title: Unbounded Knapsack Basic
hints: unlike 0/1 knapsack, an item can be reused - so the best value for capacity c might already include the very item you're deciding on
define dp[c] as the max value achievable with capacity exactly c (or less), considering all item types
for each capacity c, try every item type i whose weight fits: dp[c] = max over valid i of dp[c - weight[i]] + value[i]
build dp from capacity 0 upward - by the time you compute dp[c], every dp[c - weight[i]] for weight[i] <= c is already known, and it's fine if it reused item i itself
this is the key difference from 0/1 knapsack's 1D version: here you iterate capacity from low to high (not high to low), which is exactly what allows an item to be picked more than once
commonMistakes: iterating capacity from high to low like the 0/1 knapsack rolling array, which prevents reusing an item and silently turns this into 0/1 knapsack
forgetting dp[0] = 0 as the base case
not skipping item weights larger than the current capacity, causing negative index access

content.problemStatement:
You're packing a bag that can hold up to a given weight `capacity`. You have a list of item types, each with a `weight` and a `value`, and an unlimited supply of every item type, so you may take as many copies of any item as you like.

**Choose a combination of items whose total weight does not exceed `capacity` that maximizes total value, and return that maximum value.**
notes: capacity leaves leftover space no item can fill exactly
a single item type whose weight exceeds capacity (it must be skipped entirely)

sampleTestCases.explanation: taking two copies of the weight-5 item uses all 10 capacity for value 7 + 7 = 14, which beats every other combination
two copies of the weight-2 item use 4 capacity for value 6; the last unit of capacity is wasted since no item is that small
no capacity means no items can be taken

optimal.time: O(n * capacity) where n is the number of item types
optimal.pattern: knapsack (unbounded, bottom-up DP over capacity, reusing items freely)

bruteForce.approach: recursively try, for each capacity, taking zero or more copies of each item type (or equivalently, at each capacity step, try adding one more copy of any item and recurse on the reduced capacity), exploring all combinations
